The call, time limits and lateness

A target does not fly by itself: you call for it with a short word such as 'pull' or 'ready'. The rules then set how fast the target must come and how much time you may take.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

Sporting™ keeps a steady rhythm, and several rules protect it. You call, and the referee relays your call to the trapper (the person who releases the targets) with a sound signal. From that signal, the target has to be in the air within 3 seconds. If it comes later, the referee calls a No Bird and the target is thrown again.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 5 · Calling for the target and the 3-second release

Compak® Sporting

In Compak® Sporting a trap can be released by hand, with a remote control or by a sonopull (a microphone system that releases the trap when it hears your call). Released by hand, the target must leave 0 to 3 seconds after you call. A sonopull always waits half a second after your call, so the timing is the same each time. International events shot in line (shooters step onto station 1 one by one and move along the line to station 5) use sonopull only. A target that leaves more than 3 seconds late, or one you did not call for, is a No Bird.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 2 · Releasing targets: manual, remote, sonopull

In both disciplines the only target you may refuse is one you did not call for: it is a No Bird.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

You may not refuse it. If it was thrown correctly and you do not fire, it is scored zero.

Compak® Sporting

You may not refuse it either. A refused single is scored zero; doubles follow the table in the rules guide.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

You have at most 15 seconds between singles or between doubles.

Compak® Sporting

You have at most 10 seconds to call, counted from the shot at the previous station's target.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

The first time you go over the limit, the referee gives a warning. After that, the red-card penalties apply (Chapter 12 · Red card on repeat at the same layout). When the referee has given a final decision, for example after you protested, you must carry on shooting within 15 seconds. If you do not, or if you stall on purpose, it counts as refusal to comply: a separate offence that the jury can sanction.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 7 · 15 seconds between targets

Compak® Sporting

The first time you go over the limit, the referee notes a warning on the score sheet. If it happens again in the same round, it is a red card: a single is scored zero, and doubles follow the table in the rules guide (Chapter 21 · Penalty table after a first warning). When the referee has given a final decision, you must carry on shooting within 10 seconds. If you do not, or if you stall on purpose, it counts as refusal to comply, which the jury can sanction.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 21 · 10 seconds to call: warning, then penalty

Tip: Many coaches suggest a short, steady pre-shot routine that fits well inside the limit. For example: step onto the stand, load when the referee allows it, take your ready position, breathe out, then call. More in Pre-shot routine: the same steps in the same order.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

Lateness: if you are missing when your squad starts, the referee calls out your name and number, three times over one minute. If you arrive while the squad is still shooting the singles on the first stand and your turn has not yet passed, you join without penalty. After that, all targets you did not shoot are zeros, and you cannot make up the missed stands later with another squad.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 16 · Late or absent shooter

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

If you were late for reasons outside your control, do not rejoin the squad in that round; appeal to the jury in writing. If the jury agrees, you shoot the round with another squad. If it refuses, each layout you did not shoot counts as 25 zeros.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 16 · Lateness beyond the shooter's control

Compak® Sporting

In Compak® Sporting you must report to the referee in good time and confirm that you are there. Besides in line, there is the by-squad format: a squad of at most six shooters shoots the round together, moving from station to station. In this format, a shooter who arrives after the squad's first call of the round gets 25 zeros for that round. An appeal is made in writing to the jury, on the same day.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 9 · Late in squad shooting: 25 zeros

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

Be ready within 15 minutes of the call. If you are not there, you are disqualified.

Compak® Sporting

Be ready within 15 minutes of the call. If you are absent, you are treated as having withdrawn.

Tip: Put on hearing protection and glasses before you step onto the stand: in both disciplines a shooter without them is treated as absent (Dress code and safety on the stand).

Key points

  • A target released more than 3 seconds late is a No Bird, in both disciplines.
  • You may not refuse a target you called for; one you did not call for is a No Bird.
  • Sporting™: at most 15 seconds between singles or between doubles. Compak® Sporting: at most 10 seconds to call, counted from the shot at the previous station's target.
  • Over the time limit, the first time brings a warning and a repeat brings a red card.
  • Be on time: in Sporting™ targets missed through lateness are zero; in Compak® Sporting by squad, coming after the squad's first call costs 25 zeros.

Did you know?

In Compak® Sporting in line you count as late once your number has been taken off in the scoring computer and the next shooter is already standing on station 1.

Stand Talk

  • Referee Shooter number twenty-three!

    Meaning: Referee calling a missing shooter (three times within a minute).

  • Referee Watch your time.

    Meaning: Reminder of the 15-second limit between targets.

  • Referee Over fifteen seconds. This is a warning.

    Meaning: First time over the limit: warning; next time a penalty.

  • Referee Glasses on, or you can't shoot.

    Meaning: Without eye protection the shooter is treated as absent.

  • Referee Ten seconds, call your target.

    Meaning: Reminder of the 10-second limit to call.

  • Referee Warning: time.

    Meaning: First time over 10 seconds; noted on the score sheet.

For the interpreter
  • Do not hold the squad up with a long translation: keep it short now and give the details after the stand.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. Within how many seconds of the call must the target be released?

    1. 3 seconds
    2. 10 seconds
    3. 15 seconds
    Answer

    3 seconds

    In both disciplines a target released more than 3 seconds late is a No Bird.

    Chapter 5 · Calling for the target and the 3-second release

  2. How long do you have to call in Compak® Sporting?

    1. 5 seconds
    2. 10 seconds
    3. 30 seconds
    Answer

    10 seconds

    You have at most 10 seconds to call, counted from the shot at the previous station's target. In Sporting™ you have at most 15 seconds between singles or between doubles.

    Chapter 21 · 10 seconds to call: warning, then penalty

  3. A target is released although you did not call for it. What is it?

    1. It is a zero
    2. A yellow card
    3. It is a No Bird
    Answer

    It is a No Bird

    A target you did not call for is a No Bird, and it is the only kind you may refuse.

    Chapter 5 · Refusing a target; who rules on trajectories
